plan.title: bug(hooks): in-PR completion (#6277) moves the brief out of active/, so the #6379 binding refuses the product commit

narratives.Description: In-PR completion (#6277) moves the story brief from xbrief/active/ to xbrief/completed/ inside the product PR, and the #6379 worktree story binding then refuses that commit and every later Edit, Write and commit in the worktree with assigned_story_missing, whose repair text wrongly says to re-activate the brief. This story lets the binding admit the assigned story on an active-folder miss only when the assigned id matches one lands-with-product move in the worktree diff against the newest commit, among the merge base and the commits this branch adds after it, that still has the brief at its active path. The fence stays the merge-base blob when it exists and otherwise the one-PR mint gate on that same commit; the commit path keeps the implement intent ceiling, a completion already on the merge base stays refused, and no new gate or grant is added.
narratives.UserStory: As a story worker in a bound linked worktree, I want the worktree story binding to keep admitting my story after scope:complete --in-pr moves its brief to completed/, so that I can commit the product change and later review fixes without the operator running each commit by hand.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/scope/lands-with-product.ts: a bounded helper that, for each active/ brief path present in the merge-base tree or in a commit this branch adds after it and absent from the worktree, finds the newest such commit that still contains it (HEAD while the move is uncommitted), runs git diff --name-status -M against that single revision, and returns the lands-with-product moves found there with that containing commit. Commits behind the merge base are never candidates.
2. packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts resolveWorktreeStoryBinding: on an active-folder miss, admit only when exactly one such move has storyIdForBrief equal to the assigned id (never soleLandsWithProductMove); the hit carries the pre-move active path and the containing commit; env pin and spawn bound path are checked with pinNamesLandsWithProductMove; any other miss keeps today's refusal; refusals for a story moved in that diff do not name scope:activate.
3. packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts: on a moved-brief hit the write path and the commit path (evaluateProspectiveScopeCover) skip inspectActiveScope and the active-folder and running-status refuses, append no activate repair, and the commit path runs the implement intent ceiling itself.
4. packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts: the fence for a moved-brief hit is the merge-base blob of the old active path when it exists; otherwise the one-PR mint gate reads the brief from the containing commit, never the missing worktree file or the completed brief.
5. Tests: lands-with-product.test.ts, scope.test.ts, write-fence.test.ts, dispatcher-story-binding.test.ts and a git-fixture test story-binding-in-pr-completion.test.ts covering uncommitted and committed moves, merge-base and branch-added briefs, a completion already on the merge base, two moves, pins, refusal text and the intent ceiling.

narratives.Overview:
- On an active-folder miss, the binding admits the assigned story only when that story id equals storyIdForBrief of one lands-with-product move in git diff --name-status -M with no second revision against the newest commit, among the merge base and the commits this branch adds after it, whose tree still contains that brief at the active path, commits behind the merge base are not candidates, and that commit is HEAD while the move is uncommitted.
- When the merge base has the activeRel blob the fence is that blob, and when it does not the fence is the one-PR mint gate on that same containing commit, and neither the missing worktree file nor the completed brief is that mint head.
- The hit skips inspectActiveScope and the active-folder and running-status refuses, the commit path still runs the implement intent ceiling, and neither the commit path nor the write path appends the activate repair.
- Any other miss keeps today's refusal, including when the assigned id matches no such move and when the completion is already inside the merge base.
- The binding matches the assigned id and does not call soleLandsWithProductMove, so another story's move is not a new assignment.
- The env pin and the spawn bound path use pinNamesLandsWithProductMove, so a pin that still names the pre-move active path, the completed path, or the basename still names this story.
- The move oracle is that bounded containing-commit diff, so an uncommitted move and a move already committed on the branch are the same diff, and commits behind the merge base are not candidates.

## Acceptance Criteria


- Given a bound worktree whose diff against the newest in-range commit that still has the assigned brief at its active path moves that brief from active/ to completed/ as lands-with-product, whether or not that move is committed, when the worker commits or writes, then the binding admits that story.
- Given a brief whose old active path exists on the merge base, when the worker commits after that move, then the fence is that merge-base blob.
- Given a brief that was added on this branch, when the worker commits after that move, then the fence is the one-PR mint gate on the newest in-range commit that still contains the brief at its active path.
- Given a bound worktree whose assigned story has no brief in active/ and no such move in that diff, then the commit is refused as today.
- A completion already inside the merge base has no candidate, and the commit is refused as today.
- The refusal text for a story completed in that diff does not tell the author to re-activate the brief.
- A pin or spawn path that names the pre-move active path, the completed path, or the basename still selects that story.
- When more than one brief moves, the binding follows the assigned id and does not follow a different story's move.
- Given a story admitted through that move, when a non-implement slash session commits, then the implement intent ceiling still refuses the commit.

## Verdict

The premise does not bind as written. One diff already sees both states and still refuses a move that is already on the merge base. Calling that helper the way the check path does still does not admit the assigned story, and the commit refusal still says to activate the brief.

### F1 — Active-only pipeline refuses the moved brief
blocks-the-design
Evidence: `resolveWorktreeStoryBinding` scans only `listActiveLifecycleArtifacts` and, on a miss, repairs with `deft scope:activate -- <brief>` (`packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts` 1064-1081). A hit calls `evaluate`, which refuses a brief that is not in `active/` or whose `plan.status` is not `running` (`packages/core/src/preflight/evaluate.ts` 212-219 and 234-241). `complete` sets status `completed` and moves the file to `completed/` (`packages/core/src/scope/constants.ts` 32, `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts` 1020); `--in-pr` also stamps `lands-with-product` (`transition.ts` 1052-1057). After `bound`, `evaluateProspectiveScopeCover` still requires `inspectActiveScope` to be ready (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` 5408-5418). That scan is only `xbrief/active` and `vbrief/active` (`scope.ts` 420-432). The not-ready recovery is promote-then-activate (`packages/core/src/scope/transition-hint.ts` 17-20). The write gate hands the same bound path to `inspectActiveScope` (`dispatcher.ts` 2779-2799). `loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase` reads `file_scope` from the merge-base blob at the scope path and ignores the worktree copy (`packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts` 628-632 and 674-682). The completed path is not that blob. The allow list still lives at the old `active/` path.
Failure mode: Pointing the binding at the completed brief still refuses the product commit and later writes. The commit text still says to activate, which undoes the completion. The assigned story's governing allow list is not what covers the commit, so the right story stays blocked.
Disposition: On an active miss, admit only when the assigned story id equals `storyIdForBrief` of one lands-with-product move. Load the fence from that move's `activeRel` on the merge base. Do not run `evaluate` or `inspectActiveScope` for that hit, and do not append the activate repair, on the commit path or the write path. Any other miss keeps today's refuse.

### F2 — Sole move is the wrong authority
blocks-the-design
Evidence: `soleLandsWithProductMove` is null unless there is exactly one move (`packages/core/src/scope/lands-with-product.ts` 464-469). `resolveSoftMissingAcTargets` adopts that sole move as the story when `branchBind` is set (`scope.ts` 614-626). The binding already has an assigned id from the worker-auth assignment or the story-binding record (`scope.ts` 1040-1060), both under the shared git common dir. The diff is this worktree only. `pinNamesLandsWithProductMove` treats the old active path, the completed path, and the basename as the same story (`lands-with-product.ts` 441-460). The binding pin check uses `matchPinnedActiveScope` against active files only (`scope.ts` 1092-1106).
Failure mode: Adopting the sole move writes this worktree under another story's `file_scope` when the assigned brief is gone and some other brief moved, and it refuses the assigned story when two briefs moved. A pin that still names the pre-move active path, which is how `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` survives `scope:complete --in-pr`, conflicts, so the right commit stays refused.
Disposition: The move proves the assigned brief left `active/`. It is not a new assignment. Match the assigned id. Reuse `pinNamesLandsWithProductMove` for the env pin and the spawn bound path. Do not call `soleLandsWithProductMove` on this path.

### F3 — One diff already settles both states and the merge-base refusal
footnote
Evidence: `discoverLandsWithProductMoves` runs `git diff --name-status -M <merge-base>` with no second revision (`lands-with-product.ts` 408-410), the worktree against the merge base. A move only in the worktree and a move already committed on the branch are the same diff. A move already inside the merge base has no `D` or `R` of `active/` in that diff, so it is not a move (`lands-with-product.ts` 413-421). The unit test locks only the committed rename (`lands-with-product.test.ts` 370-384).
Failure mode: `git diff <base> HEAD` drops the uncommitted move. `git diff --cached` drops the move already committed on the branch. A disk scan of `completed/` with no `D` or `R` in this diff admits a story whose completion is already on the merge base.
Disposition: No lean change and no second scanner. Keep this diff as the oracle for both states and for the merge-base refusal. A lock for the uncommitted move and for the merge-base non-move is an implementation note.

Road not taken: treat a lands-with-product completed brief as `running` inside `evaluate`. That makes every preflight consumer treat a finished story as implementation-eligible, and it still does not point the fence at the merge-base `active/` blob. Flip only if a completed brief should spawn implementation. The process rule (in-PR completion only as a last commit after a clean review, no binding change) stays the smaller process and the larger cost. Flip to it if the fence cannot stay the merge-base active pre-image. It can.

metadata.issueBody:
## Problem

Two features released together in 0.129.11 conflict. In-PR completion (#6277) runs `scope:complete --in-pr`, which moves the story's brief from `xbrief/active/` to `xbrief/completed/` inside the last product PR, before that PR's commit. The worktree story binding (#6379) then resolves the assigned story only under `xbrief/active/`, finds nothing, and the commit hook refuses the product commit.

Exact refusal (2026-11-16, #6187 product worktree): "Prospective scope-cover denied (#6247): Worktree story binding refused (assigned_story_missing): assigned story «untrusted:github.issue.6319836133» matches no brief under xbrief/active/ in this worktree. Repair: activate the assigned story's brief in this worktree (`deft scope:activate -- <brief>`) (#6233)."

The suggested repair is wrong for this case: re-activating the brief undoes the completion.

## Evidence

- #6187, product worktree `ow-6187-product` bound with `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin (attempt att-8b5f17f2eb60dd2e). Staged: the fix, tests, a changelog fragment, the brief rename active -> completed, and the spec-drift row file. Commit refused as above; the operator ran the commit by hand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a bound worktree whose staged change moves the assigned story's brief from active/ to completed/ (an in-PR completion), when the worker commits, then the binding resolves the story from the brief being moved and the commit is admitted.
- Given a bound worktree whose assigned story has no brief in active/ and no staged move of it, then the commit is refused as today.
- The refusal text for a story completed in the change set does not tell the author to re-activate the brief.
